question: Should official riscv64 support initially ship only as an experimental architecture-specific tag, or may an unattested best-effort child be included in the standard version/latest/main manifests?
rationale: This changes the trust and availability contract of official release tags, and repository evidence does not establish maintainer approval for bypassing final-manifest attestation coverage.

options.title: Ship Standalone First
options.body: Publish only versioned `-riscv64` tags until provenance, Node update ownership, final-manifest verification, and release reliability are proven.

options.title: Require Full Parity
options.body: Include riscv64 in standard tags only after generating acceptable provenance and verifying the final three-platform manifest after its last mutation.

options.title: Pause Official Images
options.body: Keep the community image path and close or defer official publishing if the ongoing release and security maintenance cost is not justified.

recommendation.title: Ship Standalone First
recommendation.body: Publish only versioned `-riscv64` tags until provenance, Node update ownership, final-manifest verification, and release reliability are proven.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most directly connects onutc to the current Docker release runner, environment, and backfill contracts this decision affects.
